## Version 2026.11

This release upgrades htmx to version 4, makes Pegasus's custom middleware async-capable,
fixes a Vite config warning, and upgrades Python and JavaScript dependencies.

### htmx 4

Pegasus now uses [htmx 4](https://four.htmx.org/announcements/2026-08-28-htmx-4.0.0-is-released).
htmx 4 is a major rewrite with a lot of breaking changes, so if you've written your own htmx code,
read the [upgrading notes](#upgrading) below before you upgrade.

- **Upgraded `htmx.org` to version 4.** The websockets extension now ships with htmx, so the separate `htmx-ext-ws`
  package has been removed.
- Updated all of Pegasus's htmx templates and JavaScript to the htmx 4 syntax. This includes the employee demo,
  the htmx paginators, the app error banner, and the AI chat and group chat plugins.
- **Pegasus keeps the htmx 2 behavior of ignoring 4xx and 5xx responses.** htmx 4 swaps error responses into the
  page by default; Pegasus's `htmx.js` turns that off. Individual elements can still opt in to swapping error
  responses with `hx-status` (for example, `hx-status:422="swap:innerHTML"`).
- Fixed a bug where the chat UI could get stuck on "Connecting..." if the websocket opened before the page's
  JavaScript was ready. htmx 4 initializes sooner than htmx 2 did, which made this more likely.
- Group chat now bundles htmx with the rest of your front end, instead of loading an old version of htmx from a CDN
  on projects that didn't otherwise use htmx.
- Removed a redundant CSRF token hook from the htmx object demo. The `hx-headers` on `<body>` already handles this.

### Async-capable middleware

Pegasus's custom middleware now supports both sync and async requests natively. Before, Django had to
switch between sync and async contexts around each one when serving requests under ASGI.

- **`TeamsMiddleware` is now async-capable.** It also now leaves the current team context alone if
  `process_view` never ran, for example on a 404 where URL resolution fails.
- **`HealthCheckMiddleware`, `UserLocaleMiddleware`, and `UserTimezoneMiddleware` now use Django's `MiddlewareMixin`**,
  which makes them work with both sync and async requests. Their logic moved into `process_request` / `process_response` hooks.
- Added tests for the locale and timezone middleware under async requests, and for the team context
  on async and unresolved requests.

### Other changes

- **Upgraded Python and JavaScript dependencies**, including several major version upgrades of front end
  build tools.
- **Narrowed the GitHub social login scope from `user` to `user:email`.** The `user` scope gave your app
  read/write access to the user's whole GitHub profile, and login only needs their public profile and email addresses.
- **Renamed `vite.config.ts` to `vite.config.mts`.** This fixes a warning in Vite 8.3 about the config using ESM syntax
  in a file Node would load as CommonJS, which Vite's upcoming native config loader won't support.
  - The config now uses `import.meta.dirname` instead of `__dirname`, which isn't available in ES modules.
  - The TypeScript `module` setting in `tsconfig.json` is now `es2020` (was `es6`) so that type checking allows `import.meta`.
- Added `terser-webpack-plugin` as an explicit dev dependency on Webpack builds. `webpack.config.js` uses it, but it was
  only installed as a dependency of Webpack, which Webpack 5.108 no longer includes.
- Ran `npm audit fix` to address security advisories in Vite, PostCSS, nanoid, js-yaml, and others.
- The GitLab CI front end jobs now use the same Node version as the rest of the project (Node 24, was Node 22).
- Improved the built-in `resolve-pegasus-conflicts` skill based on feedback from real upgrades. It now catches
  colliding migrations and unexpected changes to user fields, flags package upgrades that get lost when
  taking Pegasus's lock files, and handles a few more edge cases during the merge.

### Upgrading

#### htmx 4

If you only use the htmx code that ships with Pegasus, you shouldn't need to do anything.
If you've written your own htmx code, you'll need to migrate it.
The htmx team's [What's New in htmx 4](https://four.htmx.org/docs/whats-new-in-htmx-4) guide covers the
full list of changes. Here are the ones most likely to affect a Pegasus project:

- **Attribute inheritance is now explicit.** In htmx 2, attributes like `hx-target` and `hx-swap` on a parent element
  applied to all of its children. In htmx 4 you have to add `:inherited` (e.g. `hx-target:inherited="this"`)
  for that to happen. This is the change that's easiest to miss, because templates that rely on it won't error.
  They'll just target the wrong element.
- **Event names changed** to a colon-separated style (e.g. `htmx:afterSwap` is now `htmx:after:swap`).
  Check any `addEventListener` calls and `hx-on` / `hx-trigger` attributes that use htmx events.
- **Websockets use new attributes and events.** `hx-ext="ws"` + `ws-connect` is now `hx-ws:connect`, `ws-send` is now
  `hx-ws:send`, and the event payloads have a different shape. See the [hx-ws extension docs](https://four.htmx.org/extensions/hx-ws).
  You can also remove `htmx-ext-ws` from your `package.json`.
- **Error responses aren't swapped.** As described above, Pegasus keeps the htmx 2 behavior. If you want htmx 4's
  default instead, remove the `noSwap` config and `htmx:before:swap` listener from `assets/javascript/htmx.js`.
- If you have a lot of htmx code and want to migrate gradually, the
  [htmx-2-compat extension](https://four.htmx.org/extensions/htmx-2-compat) restores the htmx 2 event names
  and implicit inheritance.

#### Other changes

- If your app calls the GitHub API with the user's login token and needs more than their profile and email, add the
  scopes you need back to the GitHub entry in `SOCIALACCOUNT_PROVIDERS` in `settings.py`.
- If you've customized `vite.config.ts`, move your changes into `vite.config.mts` and replace any uses of `__dirname`
  with `import.meta.dirname`. Then delete the old `vite.config.ts` file.
- If you've customized any of the middleware listed above, you'll need to merge your changes into the new structure.
